key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Gradual over days to weeks. LOCATION: Unilateral or bilateral chest. DURATION: Days to weeks, can be chronic. CHARACTER: Dyspnea, chest discomfort. AGGRAVATING: Lying flat, exertion. RELIEVING: Sitting upright, thoracentesis. TIMING: Chronic, persistent. SEVERITY: Moderate to severe (5-8/10). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Dyspnea, chest pain, cough, fever (if infectious), weight loss (if malignant). KEY POSITIVES: Dyspnea, chest pain, cough, fever. KEY NEGATIVES: No wheezing (unless reactive airway disease).
